spec: say shipped on the eight specs that shipped
Every spec in the repo said `approved` except two, including eight whose

could not tell you what was actually shipped, which is the same blindness
that let the verification convention's own evidence file sit blank for
five days at `approved`.

against memory: the verifier module and its workflow, the doc-parity
test, `auto_pull_source`, the source-repo branch in `get_artifact_root`,

None of the eight promises evidence — they predate the verification

prompt-feature-verification-eval-results.md: nothing stops a future spec

spec: forge-work-dir is shipped — the evidence file is filled from a live run
The spec has sat at `approved` since it was written, because its own stop
condition says nobody may call the feature working while the evidence file still
reads FILL_ME. Two controlled runs of the same disposable probe unit now fill it.

Baseline, no work_dir, from the main checkout while a worktree existed: the
writer's commit landed in the main checkout, the probe file was created there and
not in the worktree, and the worktree's HEAD never moved. That is the behavior the
feature exists to change, reproduced on purpose rather than asserted.

With work_dir set, all four parts of the criterion were read from git and from the
test's own output rather than from the agents' reports: the only commit is on the
worktree's branch, main's HEAD is identical before and after, main's working tree
is clean with the probe file absent, and the probe printed the worktree path it
ran in.

What the section on limits actually says, because it is the point of the file: the
"every commit" clause was tested against exactly one commit, since the editor
found nothing to cut in a 14-line probe and so never made a commit of its own. The
probe measures where the test ran, not where git committed — the loop's own editor
raised that during the run and it is right, so criteria 1-3 rest on git rather than
on the probe. The arms were not identical in shape. And a single obedient run looks
exactly like a run that could not have disobeyed; only repetition separates them,
and there has been none.

The probe and both scratch branches are deleted rather than left behind, since
"delete once the measurement is done" is an instruction to a human and not a
mechanism — also the editor's point.

docs: run Phase 0, and correct the instrument it proved wrong
Phase 0 was the named blocker on three decisions since 2026-07-16. It was never
runnable as written, and that — not procrastination — is why it sat undone.

It asked for per-unit editor token cost and editor_liveness/shrink_ratio "over
the existing forge runs". Neither works. The loop emits no token data at all:
zero references to metrics recording, zero metrics.json under any run dir. And
editor_liveness reads advocate-document word counts from *debate* runs, so it has
never measured the forge editor and structurally cannot.

The metric is also broken on its own terms. It reads 0% across all six session
records, which the scorecard defines as a dead cut mandate. Five of those runs are
single-iteration, so first draft is the final draft and the ratio is 0.0 by
arithmetic. The sixth reads -6.57 because scoped runs are designed to grow from a
500-word alignment doc to a full depth doc — the metric scores the intended design
as the worst result in the set.

What was recoverable is the number people actually wanted: from the 12 forge
handoffs on disk, 9 produced real cuts. The forge editor's cut mandate is alive at
75%, with zero reverts ever and a median rationale of 125 words against a 400
budget. The three exceptions genuinely open with "No edits." and reasoning, which I
checked rather than trusting a keyword match.

So the breadth valve stays rejected, but for a better reason: not "nobody ran the
baseline" but "per-unit editor cost is not instrumented" — a smaller and fixable
gap, and a build rather than a measurement.

Corrects the three scorecard places citing editor_liveness as the instrument for
forge-editor questions, since it has never measured that.

writer: source_repo_detection
Studio run from its own repo root now files artifacts in studio/output/
instead of treating its own repo as a consuming repo.

get_artifact_root() decided "this is somebody's project" partly by spotting a
bare .studio/ directory with no VERSION file. Studio's own repo has exactly
that shape — .studio/ holds update.toml and usage.log — so running
`python studio/run_phase.py <cmd>` from the repo root, the invocation CLAUDE.md
documents, made Studio classify itself as a guest. Artifacts landed in
<repo>/.studio/output/ and prepare wrote a stray docs/studio-bridge.md into the
source tree.

The new branch identifies the source repo structurally: a studio_root that is
not an installed snapshot, with cwd under its parent. It sits above the
.studio/VERSION walk-up so a source repo is recognized before any consumer
heuristic can claim it, and below --artifact-root and STUDIO_ARTIFACT_ROOT,
which are deliberate overrides and still win.

This is a restoration, not an invention. get_output_root, get_knowledge_log_path,
_project_name and get_outcomes_ledger_path all already branch on
`artifact_root == studio_root` meaning "this is the source repo", and
_project_name's docstring states the invariant outright. impl_loop.py resolves
the source repo this way already. get_artifact_root() was the outlier; the two
now agree.

Three existing cross-repo tests placed the pretend consuming repo as a sibling
of studio/, which under the new rule reads as a directory inside the Studio
source repo. Their studio_root moves one level down so the caller's repo is
genuinely outside the source tree — the layout those tests meant to describe.

Verified by reverting the branch by hand and watching the new tests go red: the
repo-root case failed and prepare printed "Created bridge doc". The
cwd == studio_root test stayed green throughout, which is the point — it proves
the new coverage cannot pass for the old reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>


writer: verification_convention


fix: close the two honesty holes the review found
Both Must-fix items from the review on #84. Both were real, both are amendments to
approved specs, and both amendments are in this commit.

A graded run with the editor off shipped clean. `editor_enabled === false` returned
the literal `flagged: false` even when the unit carried acceptance criteria, so a
`/forge --spec` run with `mandate = "off"` would log "criteria ungraded" and still
report a clean unit — nobody graded anything, and the payload said everything was
fine. This spec already refuses the same failure in its other form, ruling that a
mistyped `--spec` must stop rather than "silently downgrade to an ungraded run";
config is just a quieter way to reach the same place. Now `flagged` is true on that
path when criteria were carried, and false when they were not, so the config's
users see nothing new unless they also asked for grading.

Worth being clear about provenance: that line came from the merged per-criterion
grading work, not from this branch. The review found it here because this branch
is stacked on it.

The escalation prompt asked the writer to lie about its tests. It said to report
`tests` "honestly (passed=false and the real exit_code)" — two instructions that
cannot both be followed. A writer blocked on scope, a missing interface, or
contradictory instructions can be staring at a green suite, and telling it to claim
red corrupts the one machine-checked field in the handoff to signal something
`stuck` already says. Nothing depended on it: the entry gate closes on
`mvi_claimed=false` alone, which the JS tests already proved by handing an escalated
writer a green suite and watching the gate stay shut. The prompt now asks for the
real exit code and says outright not to report a red suite to mean "I am stuck."

Two tests, each verified by reverting the fix and watching the intended test fail.
Also corrected the three other places that described `tests.passed=false` as part
of the escalation record; the signal is the `writer(stuck):` label, `mvi_claimed`,
and `stuck`.

Suite 831.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>


editor: entry_gate_pinned


writer: entry_gate_pinned


editor: writer_escalation


writer: writer_escalation


fix: the gate matches each criterion instead of counting the grades
Two reviewers went over the previous commit — which had never had an adversarial
pass, since I wrote it by hand outside the loop — and both found real problems.

The gate counted grades instead of matching them. Three verdicts that all named
the same easy criterion, all passing, would hold the gate on a unit whose other
two criteria were never looked at. That is the hallucinated-or-softened-criterion
risk the spec already names, arriving through the check meant to catch it. The
gate now requires every criterion to be matched, by its own text, to a passing
grade that carries evidence — which also fixes the mirror case, where a Build
Plan listing one criterion twice flagged an honest single verdict. Verdicts
naming criteria the unit never carried are ignored rather than punished.

A pass with the evidence field left blank no longer counts. The schema requires
the field, but an empty string satisfies it, so without this the field deterred
nothing. Enforced at the gate rather than with a schema minLength, so a bluff
gets the unit flagged instead of rejecting the whole payload and killing the
editor stage.

No test could see the gate. It was an inline expression, so neutralizing the
criteria check left all 28 tests green — an enforcement mechanism no test can
reach is not enforcement. It is now a named function with its own tests, the same
pattern collectReviewerConcerns already uses.

The spec's decision table still ruled "no new gate — the exit gate's code is
untouched", which the previous commit had already made false. Amended, along with
the reworded criterion 2, which undercounted the editor prompt's additions.

Also cut: five copies of the same justification, down to one in the spec and a
short pointer at each use. The two criteria log lines collapse into one, which
fixes a spec-less run logging "Criteria not passing" while shipping unflagged,
and a "graded 4/3 — an ungraded criterion" line that misreported over-grading.

Mutations verified, each caught by the test meant to catch it: neutralizing the
gate's criteria check, regressing the rule to a count, and dropping the evidence
requirement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>


editor: loop_grades_criteria


writer: loop_grades_criteria


spec: named-risk valve for the /forge editor's read scope
The editor is told "Do not wander beyond that read scope" with no exception.
That leaves one class of bug unfindable: code that depends on other code
without importing it. Rename a config key, change a file format, alter a CLI
flag, and every test passes because nothing in the import graph noticed. The
editor is the only agent positioned to catch it and is forbidden to look.

This replaces the ban with a valve — open one more file, but only against a
risk you can name, one file per risk, and report what you checked including
the clean checks. Reads widen; edits do not.

The contrarian earned its rejection twice over. It killed the rationale the
first draft rested on: the ban does not orphan the existing out_of_unit_scope
concern category, because read scope is larger than unit scope, and that false
claim was about to be committed into the design of record. The true argument is
narrower — direct importers only catch static-import consumers.

It also caught that the "cite, don't narrate" rule illustrated itself with a
fabricated citation: studio/verdict.py is 7 lines long and the example pointed
at line 88. A rule against asserting what you cannot point at, modelling a made
-up pointer. The example is deleted and the spec records why nobody should add
it back.

Also cut: three of five proposed tests (one passed before the change, one was
unfalsifiable, one forbade a decision that was never forbidden), and a plan to
hand-record two token numbers as the valve's first data points — the spec
already calls two data points insufficient, so two more would assert precision
it disclaims. A one-line provenance note replaces them.

writer: unit_impl_loop_config


feat: add implementation writer/editor loop (spec + workflow + /studio-implement)
Brings the advocate/contrarian (writer/editor) cadence into implementation: a
writer agent builds one complete MVI unit and commits its passing state; a fresh
editor agent (reusing CONTRARIAN_MANDATE) cuts/refines against the writer's diff,
reverting if an edit breaks green; then the unit is delivered.

- studio/docs/IMPLEMENTATION_LOOP_SPEC.md — design spec. Gate split into an entry
  moment (writer declares done + tests green -> triggers editor) and an exit moment
  (editor's authoritative MVI verdict can overturn the claim). Prompts/gates/cadence/
  handoff kept as data so a port rewrites only the thin shell. Refined once via a
  Product + Engineering role pass.
- .claude/workflows/implementation-loop.js — the orchestration shell (not yet run).
  In-memory handoff anchored to writer_sha for diff base + revert point.
- .claude/commands/studio-implement.md — /studio-implement: parse request -> echo
  plan -> run the loop. The authorized trigger that opts in to the workflow.
- .gitignore — track .claude/workflows/ (parallel to the existing commands exception)
  so the command's workflow ships with it.
